examples.en: Every morning my mom packs my lunch box.

examples.ko: 내일 소풍 가니까 김밥을 싸 주세요.
examples.en: We're going on a picnic tomorrow, so please make and pack kimbap.
I wrapped my friend's present in pretty paper.

examples.ko: 내일 여행을 가서 오늘 짐을 싸야 해요.
examples.en: I'm going on a trip tomorrow, so I have to pack my bags today.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 여행 가방을 싸고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm packing my travel bag right now.
I packed a sandwich and brought it to eat for lunch.

explain: '도시락을 싸다', '짐을 싸다'처럼 목적어가 있는 동사예요. 값이 '싸요'(cheap)와 모양이 같으니 앞말을 보세요. 먹다 남은 음식을 가져갈 때도 '싸 주세요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 소풍 때문에 아침 일찍 김밥을 싸요.
phrases.en: I make gimbap early in the morning because of the picnic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김에 밥과 재료를 넣어 말아서 김밥을 만들 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rolling rice and fillings in seaweed to make gimbap.

explain_en: It is a verb that takes an object, as in '도시락을 싸다' and '짐을 싸다'. It looks the same as '싸요' (cheap), so check the word before it. People also say '싸 주세요' when asking for leftovers to take home.

examples.en: Please write your name and age at the top of the application.
Sorry, but could you write your phone number on a memo pad?

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 선생님 말씀을 다 적었어요.
examples.en: I wrote down everything the teacher said in class.
I wrote the appointment time down on the calendar.

examples.ko: 주소를 잘못 적어서 택배가 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I wrote the address wrong, so the package didn't arrive.
What are you writing in your notebook right now?

explain: 이름, 주소, 전화번호처럼 짧은 정보를 적어 둘 때 어울려요. 편지나 일기, 글을 쓸 때는 '쓰다'가 더 자연스러워요. '적어요'는 '돈이 적어요'(few)와 모양이 같지만 '을/를' 목적어가 있으면 '적다'(write)예요.

phrases.example: 수업 시간에 선생님 말씀을 받아 적어요.
phrases.en: In class, I write down what the teacher says.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 말하는 내용을 듣고 그대로 적을 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when writing down what someone is saying as they say it.

explain_en: It fits when you write down short information like a name, address or phone number. For letters, diaries or longer writing, '쓰다' sounds more natural. '적어요' looks the same as in '돈이 적어요' (little money), but with an object marked by '을/를' it means 'write down'.
